story:
A tree from the Argentine pampas grows on a rock in the Adriatic. The ombu, Phytolacca dioica, is native to South America, and Puglia's register of monumental trees lists a group of them on Isola San Nicola, the fortified island of the Tremiti, on sheet 01/E363/FG/16.

The register calls it a homogeneous group rather than one tree, and it gives no girth, no height and no age. What it records is that ombu here are worth protecting. The species is an odd one to find on a Mediterranean island, evergreen, with a swollen, buttressed base, and it stands up well to sea wind.

The proof that they are still there is recent. In August 2025 two visitors, three weeks apart, logged an ombu on San Nicola on iNaturalist, each identification confirmed by a second person, and their two GPS points fall about 18 metres apart and within about 30 metres of the register's coordinate. That points to one small cluster.

What we cannot tell you yet is whether that spot is on a public path or inside a closed part of the abbey and fortress that cover the island. Ferries and hydrofoils run to San Nicola in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico, thinning out outside May to September.

Nobody has published an age for these trees. If you go, tell us which trunk is biggest and how you reached it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the base, swollen and buttressed, on an evergreen tree from South America. It stands in a small cluster of ombu on Isola San Nicola, the island of the abbey and fortress.
name: Ombu of San Nicola, Isole Tremiti
access: Island of San Nicola is open to visitors by ferry/hydrofoil (Termoli, Vieste, Peschici, Rodi Garganico, Manfredonia in season). Whether the exact tree stands on a public path or inside a paid or closed part of the abbey-fortress complex is NOT established; flagged.
transport: Ferry or hydrofoil to San Nicola in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico (about 45 to 90 minutes depending on port); services thin out outside May to September. Over 30 minutes, so an island day trip, not a walk from the coast.
verify_notes: SOURCES: Puglia register 01/E363/FG/16 records an 'insieme omogeneo di Phytolacca dioica' (a homogeneous group, not a single measured tree) on Isola San Nicola, no girth or height given. ALIVE and species: two independent iNaturalist observers recorded Phytolacca dioica on San Nicola in 2025 (obs 303541268, 2025-08-02, 42.120369,15.503167; obs 309180835, 2025-08-26, 42.120531,15.503119), each confirmed by a second identifier, marked casual (cultivated); both within about 30 m of the register point and about 18 m of each other. Photos CC BY-NC (not usable). Web searches found no article, plaque or guide naming this ombu; only the register and iNaturalist. Ombu is a non-native South American tree, so on a Tremiti page its interest is the oddity (swollen buttressed base, evergreen, resists sea wind); no age basis, left empty. Group, not single tree: the exact trunk to stand at is not established, so approximate; two GPS fixes of the species ~18 m apart suggests one small cluster. Access to the exact spot unverified.

No measurement or age, so nothing a story could stand on beyond the species. Ships with a GPS fix and a photo from a public path.
